en.title: GTA 6 TV Spot Ditches Steamy Scenes, Hints at PlayStation's Marketing Dominance
en.summary: The first television commercial for Grand Theft Auto VI has aired, featuring subtle but significant changes from its initial launch trailer. Notably, intimate moments have been removed, while platform exclusivity messaging appears to be sharpened.
en.body:
Rockstar Games has unveiled the first official television commercial for the highly anticipated **Grand Theft Auto VI**, and it comes with a few notable adjustments. While largely mirroring the widely seen launch trailer, this 90-second spot, which aired during NBC Sports programming, omits several intimate scenes, particularly those involving **Lucia** and **Jason** in a shower setting. These cuts, while seemingly minor, result in slightly extended footage in other areas, offering fans a few precious extra milliseconds of Vice City mayhem.

Beyond the removal of steamy moments, the commercial also makes a significant statement regarding platform marketing. The **Xbox** logo has been conspicuously absent from this TV spot. This omission is a clear indicator of the extensive marketing deal between Rockstar Games and Sony, which has positioned the **PlayStation 5** as the premier platform for **GTA VI**. Trailers and gameplay demonstrations have consistently featured PS5 capture, and messaging has often emphasized it as "the best place to play." For casual viewers encountering the game for the first time through this advert, the implication could be that **PlayStation** is the sole destination for **Rockstar**'s latest open-world crime saga, a narrative Sony is undoubtedly keen to promote.

## A Closer Look at Vice City's Visuals

While the narrative focus shifts towards platform exclusivity, the commercial still provides glimpses into the stunning visual fidelity that **Grand Theft Auto VI** promises. The detailed character models, particularly **Lucia**'s meticulously rendered hair, showcase the advanced graphical technology at play. This "fancy hair tech," as some fans have dubbed it, is a testament to the developers' commitment to pushing visual boundaries. The extended shots, whether of the plane or **Jason** and **Lucia**, allow for a deeper appreciation of the environments and character animations, hinting at the immersive world players will soon explore. The sheer quality of the graphics suggests a game built with longevity in mind, potentially setting a new benchmark for open-world experiences.

## Community Buzz and Platform Wars

The changes in the TV commercial have naturally sparked discussion within the **GTA** community. The removal of the shower scenes has led to speculation, though no definitive reason has been provided by **Rockstar**. More significantly, the absence of the **Xbox** logo fuels the ongoing conversation about platform exclusivity and marketing power plays in the gaming industry. This aggressive positioning by Sony, leveraging **GTA VI** as a key exclusive marketing asset, is a strategy that resonates deeply with core gamers who understand the implications for console sales and visibility. It also raises questions for **Xbox** fans about how **Rockstar** will address their platform in future marketing efforts, especially given the game's confirmed multi-platform release on both **PlayStation 5** and **Xbox Series X/S**.

## What's Next

With **Grand Theft Auto VI** slated for release next month on **PlayStation 5** and **Xbox Series X/S**, expect further marketing pushes from all involved parties. The ongoing negotiation of platform visibility will likely continue to shape how the game is presented to the public leading up to its launch.

content_raw: GTA 6 has its first TV commercial, and it's a little different than the launch trailer. The 90-second GTA 6 advert, which was spotted on NBC Sports, is for the most part the launch trailer Rockstar Games released last week, but the shower smooching scenes have been taken out. All three of them. Luckily, that means some of the other scenes are slightly extended, giving us a few milliseconds of extra footage. This is further evidence of the extensive partnership between Sony and Rockstar for GTA 6 marketing rights, which has seen official trailers and the extended gameplay look feature gameplay captured from PS5, and messaging that calls PS5 “the best place to play.” More casual fans who might discover that GTA 6 is coming out at all from an advert on something like live sports might reasonably conclude that PlayStation is the only place to play Rockstar’s open world crime sequel, which is no doubt what Sony's hoping for from its partnership. Last month, Microsoft stepped in to address a report that claimed GTA 6 preorders were “heavily skewed” toward PS5 over Xbox Series X and S. In a report about recent layoffs and studio reorganization at Xbox , The Verge’s Tom Warren said the PS5’s dominance over GTA 6 preorders was “ringing yet more alarm bells" about Xbox as a platform. However, Xbox CSO Matthew Ball insisted that Microsoft was “very happy” with GTA 6 preorders, and that its internal data showed preorders were matching “our share of the console market.” Sony has published blog posts talking about the features of the PS5 that GTA 6 will use, such as the speaker in the DualSense controller and the pad's haptic feedback. Other additions to GTA 6's PS5 marketing campaign include a version of the PlayStation app logo on smartphones that features GTA 6 t come as much of a surprise. Miami is currently completely taken over by the game, which is set in a fictionalized Miami called Vice City, as well as the surrounding area. Yesterday, people spotted GTA 6 Burger Shot restaurants pop up in the Kaseya Center. Fans also recently spotted flashy GTA-branded sports cars driving around Miami . The cars were seen with camera crews, suggesting some kind of live-action advertising is happening for GTA 6.
